The chair wishes to place on record and remind the counsel for both parties and our distinguished senator-judges, including the presiding officer, that while every witness takes an oath before this court to

Report correction
Source ↗

Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero

S00009

testify truthfully to answer all questions, the witness remains entitled to the rights enumerated under Rule 1323, Section 3 of the Rules on Evidence. which has suppletory application to these proceedings. The Chair would like to spread into the records the provisions of Section 3. Section 3. Rights and Obligations of Witnesses. A witness must answer questions, although his answer may tend to establish a claim against him. However, it is the right of a witness, number one, To be protected from irrelevant, improper or insulting questions and from harsh or insulting demeanor. Not to be detained any longer than the interest of justice require. Not to be examined except only as to matters pertinent to the issue. Not to give an answer which will tend to subject him or her to a penalty for an offense unless otherwise provided by law.

Report correction
Source ↗

Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero

S00010

Not to give an answer which will tend to degrade his reputation unless it is to be the very fact at issue or to a fact from which the fact in issue would be presumed. But a witness must answer to the fact of his previous final conviction for an offense. The Chair wishes to emphasize that an answer which may be unsatisfactory is not inherently contemptible. Supreme Court cases have cautioned courts to use the power of contempt with the highest restraint. The Chair wishes to remind the members of this Court as well, including the Presiding Officer himself, who stated that his patience was wearing thin the other day, that we are sitting as Senator judges in a trial. Our rules behoove us to receive and evaluate the evidence with impartiality and due to the often lengthy examination by both parties with utmost patience as well. I wish to also remind the counsel for both parties as well as our fellow senator judges including this representation that while we may rigorously examine witnesses and test the credibility of their testimonies, we must refrain from resorting to a manner of questioning or to making declarations that elicit fear rather than candor. The Chair therefore respectfully requests our distinguished colleagues, the councils for the parties including this representation, to exercise restraint expected of us. Unlike in inquiries in aid of legislation, an answer of I do not know or I do not recall may be extremely frustrating. It's one that we may encounter numerous times in a proceeding such as this. What we can control, however, is how we appreciate and weigh the testimonies and statements delivered before this Court. We owe it to the parties, to the witnesses, and to the institution we represent to conduct the proceedings still with fairness, dignity, and respect in spite and despite our frustration and or disappointment with what the witness may or may not be saying.
